findings.evidence: "the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month"
findings.fix: Pick one owner and one cadence for the equipment catalog and state it once; remove or reconcile the duplicate claims in "Special Cases" and "Questions and Updates."
findings.location: Program Overview, paragraph 2 ("Similarly, the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog...")
findings.violation: This directly conflicts with the "Special Cases" section ("The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year") and the "Questions and Updates" section ("The benefits team reviews the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year") - three different owners and two different cadences are given for the same artifact.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Name the specific clock explicitly (e.g., "the 90-day eligibility period" or "the benefit-year claim window").
findings.location: Eligibility, paragraph 2 ("The stipend clock resumes on their first day back.")
findings.violation: "Stipend clock" is never defined - it's unclear whether this refers to the 90-day continuous-service requirement or the benefit-year claim window, so readers can't determine what actually resumes.

findings.evidence: "one claim per employee per benefit year" vs. "one device per category per employee"
findings.fix: Add a time scope to the device-per-category rule (e.g., "one device per category per benefit year") or clarify how it relates to the one-claim-per-year rule.
findings.location: Eligibility ("The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year.") vs. Restrictions and Exceptions ("the policy applies to one device per category per employee.")
findings.violation: It's unclear whether the per-category device limit is annual (consistent with the yearly claim) or a lifetime limit, creating a potential contradiction about how often equipment can be reimbursed.

findings.fix: Specify which request types require more than a photo receipt, or remove the qualifier if none exist.
findings.location: Required Documentation, paragraph 1 ("A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests.")
findings.violation: The exceptions to this rule are never identified, leaving employees unable to know when a photo receipt is insufficient.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person, e.g., "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This sentence switches to second-person voice ("you"/"we"), breaking from the third-person voice ("employees," "the manager," "the finance office") used everywhere else in the document.

findings.evidence: "Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Rename the section to reflect its actual content (e.g., "Reconciliation Process") or move this content under an existing process section.
findings.location: Terminology Notes, section heading and body
findings.violation: The section is titled "Terminology Notes" but contains no term definitions - it describes a process flow, so the heading doesn't match the content.

findings.evidence: "Payroll releases the stipend item amount" vs. "The finance office deposits the amount"
findings.fix: Identify a single responsible party for disbursement and use that name consistently throughout.
findings.location: Terminology Notes ("Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review.") vs. Reimbursement Amounts ("The finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle.")
findings.violation: Two different sections name different parties (payroll vs. finance office) as responsible for disbursing the stipend, which is contradictory.

findings.evidence: "you submit the request in the portal. You track its status"
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person and remove the duplicate restatement of the "How to Apply" content, or cross-reference it instead of repeating it.
findings.location: Terminology Notes, last paragraph ("Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears.")
findings.violation: This again shifts to second-person voice, inconsistent with the third-person voice used elsewhere, and redundantly restates content already covered in "How to Apply."

findings.evidence: "begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt"
findings.fix: List the complete, ordered set of steps and align the sequence with the "How to Apply" section.
findings.location: Request Steps ("Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt.")
findings.violation: This two-item list appears truncated - it omits intermediate steps (e.g., selecting equipment, submitting for approval) described elsewhere, and its stated starting point ("confirming eligibility") doesn't match the sequence given in "How to Apply," which starts with the portal request itself.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Reconcile ownership and cadence of the equipment catalog across all sections that mention it.
findings.location: Special Cases ("The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year.")
findings.violation: This contradicts Program Overview, which attributes equipment catalog updates to the IT asset group on a monthly cadence, not to a finance liaison at fiscal-year start.

findings.evidence: "flags any request that repeats within the same quarter"
findings.fix: Clarify under what circumstances a repeat request within a quarter is possible (e.g., multiple device categories) or remove this flagging rule if it cannot occur.
findings.location: Review Responsibility ("The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter.")
findings.violation: This implies multiple stipend requests can occur within the same quarter/year, which contradicts the Eligibility section's statement that the stipend covers only "one claim per employee per benefit year."

findings.evidence: "The benefits team reviews the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Consolidate all equipment-catalog maintenance statements into a single authoritative sentence stated once in the document.
findings.location: Questions and Updates ("The benefits team reviews the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year.")
findings.violation: This is a third, conflicting account of who maintains the equipment catalog and when, differing from both Program Overview (IT asset group, monthly) and Special Cases (finance liaison, fiscal-year start).
